title: 1962 AHSME Problem 15
statement: Given triangle \(ABC\) with base \(AB\) fixed in length and position. As the vertex \(C\) moves on a straight line, the intersection point of the three medians moves on:

solutions.text:
Let \(A,\) \(B,\) and \(C\) also denote their position vectors. The centroid is \[ G=\frac{A+B+C}{3}. \] Since \(A\) and \(B\) are fixed, this is a translation and scaling by \(\frac{1}{3}\) of the position of \(C.\) A straight-line locus therefore maps to a straight-line locus.

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: The centroid lies two-thirds of the way from a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side
With \(AB\) fixed, express the centroid as a fixed point plus one-third of the position vector of \(C\)
